paragraphs: AirSight sells a drone detection software platform called AirGuard that gives security teams the real-time location of drones and of their pilots. Detection layers offered are Remote ID, RF and DF, radar and camera. The company does not build the sensors itself and describes itself as a software and systems integration business that sources hardware from partners.

The site describes buyers including airports, stadiums, prisons, universities, army bases and Fortune 500 companies. Case files name the University of Kentucky, Camping World Stadium and the Chula Vista Police Department, whose own drone flights get third-party tracking. A Complete Tier adds radar for drones that do not transmit signals, plus staff who visually confirm alerts around the clock.

AirSight was established in 2003 as 911Security. Robert Tabbara, its President and Owner, started the business after the attacks of 9/11 2001. The move into drone detection software came in July 2019. Headquarters is in Dallas, TX, with offices in Chicago, IL and Pune, India, and the company is a registered Small Business Enterprise and Public Works Contractor.

quote.text: AirSight empowers security leaders to strengthen the Day-to-Day security at their organizations.
